{{Quote|I think I've found the perfect place. Remote. A bit desolate, but tranquil.|Saw Gerrera to the Ersos, referring to Lah'mu|<ref name="Catalyst" />}}
'''Lah'mu''' was a [[Planetary ring|ringed]] agrarian [[planet]] in the [[Raioballo sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. Its small population of settlers included the [[Erso family]], who relocated to Lah'mu after the [[Clone Wars]], and were ultimately tracked down by [[Director]] [[Orson Callan Krennic]] [[Standard year|years]] later.

==Description==
{{Quote|It looks unspoiled.|Galen Walton Erso|<ref name="Catalyst" />}}
[[File:Lahmu_Databank.jpg|thumb|left||192px|Krennic's [[Delta-class T-3c shuttle|shuttle]] at the Erso homestead]]
Lah'mu was an inaccessible [[planet]]<ref name="UVG" /> located in the [[Raioballo sector]]<ref name="RO World Locations" /> of [[the galaxy]]'s [[Outer Rim Territories]], far from major [[hyperspace route]]s. Its [[planetary ring]]s were primarily silica formed from the remains of one of the planet's ancient [[moon]]s, pulverized long before the [[Clone Wars]]. Lah'mu retained one other natural satellite.<ref name="UVG" />

The planet itself was lush and dark green in color,<ref name="Rogue One" /> and its biosphere transformed [[iron]] into [[chlorophyll]].<ref name="UVG" /> The climate was rainy.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> The planet's crust, which split numerous times during its early geological life, was fertile and rich with minerals and soils brought to the surface during this turbulent period. These substances, including [[zinc]], [[chlorine]], [[cobalt]], [[nitrogen]], and [[boron]], rendered the [[Water|groundwater]] unpleasant to drink, despite the presence of an abundant [[hydrosphere]]. Further, volcanic [[tephra]] contaminated the greenery.<ref name="UVG" /> Part of the reason for the rainfall and high mineral content was due to heavy volcanic and geothermal activity, especially in the Eastern hemisphere.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" />

[[File:Lahmu-R1.png|thumb|right|242px|Lah'mu's planetary rings]]
Verdant and tranquil, Lah'mu's surface hosted [[mountain]] peaks and plateaus, including some [[volcano]]es, [[Color|black]] sand beaches, saline seas, geysers, and farmlands. Settlers lived on the western hemisphere, particularly around the fertile lowlands.<ref name="UVG" />

==History==
Lah'mu was named from a [[Pak Pak|Neimoidian]] word meaning "prosperity." Early in its geographic life, Lah'mu's crust split numerous times, bringing minerals and soils to the surface that would later be farmed by the planet's sparse settlers. Initially hosting several [[moon]]s, Lah'mu gained a planetary ring after one ancient satellite was pulverized, its remaining material pulled into orbit to form silica rings that cast shadows across the planet's surface. [[Volcano]]es ejected tephra during this formative period, contaminating Lah'mu's natural greenery, forcing later settlers to carefully sift the soil.<ref name="UVG" />

[[File:Lahmu-ROUVG.png|thumb|left|250px|Lah'mu was a focus of the Republic Ministry of Economic Development]]
During the last [[Standard decade|decades]] of the [[Galactic Republic]], the [[Republic Ministry of Economic Development|Ministry of Economic Development]] encouraged citizens to relocate to worlds such as Lah'mu in the Outer Rim Territories, and offered incentives such as land parcels for the development of homesteads. Although the effort was mismanaged and saw many worlds either sparsely populated or abandoned, Lah'mu was deemed safe if otherwise forgotten.<ref name="UVG" />

At some point before [[40 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' places the events of ''[[Master & Apprentice]]'' in [[40 BBY]].</ref> the [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] visited a royal [[chief]]'s [[Chief's fortress|fortress]] on Lah'mu with his [[Jedi Master|Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]].<ref name="Master & Apprentice" />

As of [[13 BBY]], Lah'mu hosted fewer than five hundred settlers, occupying farmlands on the western hemisphere. Many of these individuals arrived on Lah'mu seeking to avoid war; among them were the [[Erso family]], whose association with [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]] during the [[Clone Wars]] forced them into hiding on the remote, inaccessible world. [[Galen Walton Erso|Galen]] and [[Lyra Erso]] chose to reside in a sixty-five hectare [[Erso homestead|homestead]] on the planet's less popular eastern side, purchased with the assistance of [[Saw Gerrera]]. The Ersos grew crops and utilized [[Pretormin Environmental Corporation]] [[GX-8 water vaporator]]s to distill water vapor from the air.<ref name="UVG" />

[[File:Lahmu_EW.png|thumb|right|250px|Death troopers at the Erso homestead]]
Unfortunately for the family, [[Director]] Krennic ultimately tracked them down, and arrived on Lah'mu to [[Capture of Galen Erso|take]] Galen, Lyra, and their young daughter [[Jyn Erso|Jyn]], with him to ensure the completion of his stalled [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[Project Stardust|project]]. Galen refused, and a brief firefight erupted in which Krennic was dealt a glancing blow and Lyra was shot dead. [[Krennic's guard squadron|Krennic's]] [[death trooper]]s burned the homestead and took Galen into custody, while Jyn fled to the black gulch beyond the former homestead's edge. There, she secreted herself in a shelter beneath a hidden hatch camouflaged by an artificial rock. She was later rescued by Gerrera.<ref name="Rogue One" />

==Inhabitants==
Lah'mu was sparsely populated, home to under five hundred [[human]] settlers who lived on verdant, tranquil farmlands across the western hemisphere. Most of the population came to the planet to avoid the [[Clone Wars]], through encouragement from the [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] Ministry of Economic Development.<ref name="UVG" /> Part of the reason for this sparse settling was because Lah'mu was too far from [[hyperspace route]]s.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> The planet had no known indigenous intelligent life.<ref name="UVG" />

==Behind the scenes==
Lah'mu was created for the [[2016]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. [[Wikipedia:Lahmu|Lahmu]] is a [[Wikipedia:Mesopotamian mythology|Mesopotamian]] deity associated with agriculture.<ref name="Lahmu">{{WebCite|url=https://www.etymonline.com/word/Bethlehem#etymonline_v_30442|text=Bethlehem|work=[[Wikipedia:Online Etymology Dictionary|Online Etymology Dictionary]]|archivedate=20240114232935}}</ref>
